% imakeidx's indexes printed from an \include file, each with its .ind
% beside the document from an earlier build: a named index after
% \indexprologue, the main index while a named index is printed in the
% main file, a named index printed from a file that the \include file
% reads with \input, and a named index whose option -l reaches makeindex.
% The index of places is printed in the main file.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{imakeidx}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\makeindex
\makeindex[name=test-staleaux-ind-incl-people,title=Index of people]
\makeindex[name=test-staleaux-ind-incl-terms,title=Index of terms]
\makeindex[name=test-staleaux-ind-incl-words,title=Index of words,options=-l]
\makeindex[name=test-staleaux-ind-incl-places,title=Index of places]
\begin{document}
An apple\index{Apple}, after Euler\index[test-staleaux-ind-incl-people]{Euler}, is a fruit\index[test-staleaux-ind-incl-terms]{Fruit} from Basel\index[test-staleaux-ind-incl-places]{Basel}.
Ice cream\index[test-staleaux-ind-incl-words]{Ice cream} and an iceberg\index[test-staleaux-ind-incl-words]{Iceberg}.
\include{test-staleaux-ind-incl/back}
\printindex[test-staleaux-ind-incl-places]
